knowledge_abstraction.bug_theme: Layout-dependent numerical inconsistency for reduction-style operators
knowledge_abstraction.general_principle: Floating-point reduction operations can produce different rounding results when logically equivalent tensor layouts cause different memory traversal and accumulation orders.

risk_dimensions.shape: Reduction dimensions that can be permuted or transposed while preserving logical semantics
risk_dimensions.dtype: Floating-point dtypes where rounding error is observable, especially float32 and float64
risk_dimensions.memory: Non-contiguous, permuted, or transposed tensor layouts
risk_dimensions.device: CPU and other backends where reduction order may depend on memory layout

failure_mechanism.description: Equivalent tensor layouts can change the order of floating-point accumulation in reduction kernels, leading to small numerical differences that violate strict correctness expectations.

input_exploration: Explore tensors with permuted, transposed, or otherwise non-contiguous memory layouts
Vary floating-point dtypes and value distributions, including large dynamic range and negative values
Compare results from logically equivalent layout transformations before and after reduction
constraint_awareness: Keep the logical reduction dimension and dtype identical across compared variants
Ensure identical input values are used for all layout transformations
oracle_strategy: Compare outputs from equivalent layout transformations using max absolute difference and flag differences above a strict tolerance

transferability.reason: The principle applies broadly to reduction and layout-sensitive operations where floating-point accumulation order may change with memory traversal order, not just to the original softmax API.

important_considerations: Test operations whose results depend on reduction order and floating-point accumulation
Introduce permute, transpose, and inverse-permute layout variations
Compare logically equivalent computations with strict numerical oracles
generation_strategy: Generate harnesses that create a base tensor, apply inverse layout transformations before and after an operation under test, and check whether outputs differ beyond a strict tolerance.
